limit.addressed_by: ruling 7's last_statement count: in both examples the last statement's region does not count the early returns
limit.at_0_16_27: no sub-test body executed a `return` region in any step (early_returns_executed is empty for every call), and no sub-test returns a value, so no `?` exit exists; the baseline verdicts are therefore completions
limit.finding: the closing-brace exit region also counts early returns: rustc routes every `return` of a body through its one return block, whose span is the closing brace. So the rule separates a completed or early-returned body from a panicked or never-entered one, but not a completed body from one that returned early.

locator_limits.matches_macro: a statement that is or holds a `matches!` call has no region that counts arrivals: the expansion maps its arm regions onto the call site. Three helpers read as not executed for this reason (entered_class locator_limit): tests/src/jmap/mail/acl.rs assert_forbidden, tests/src/smtp/inbound/mod.rs is_reload_settings and is_refresh. No sub-test is affected. Counting the highest region anywhere in the statement instead would treat them as executed and changes no sub-test verdict, but it departs from ruling 7's wording, so it is not done here.

method.body_record_async: rustc emits two records per async fn. The outer one (v0 symbol `_RNv...4test`) has one region from the start of the signature to just before the body's opening brace. The body is a closure record (v0 symbol prefix `_RNC`, `..4test0B7_`) whose first region is the opening brace `{` itself. Take the `_RNC` record whose first region starts exactly at the body's opening brace (line, column from the source with comments and literals blanked).
method.body_record_plain: the record that is not a closure (no `_RNC` prefix) whose first region (the signature, e.g. `pub fn test()`) starts on the line of the `fn` keyword.
method.both_binaries: each test-crate function appears twice (build-A, the unified workspace binary, and build-B, the `-p tests` binary that the suites run); one record must satisfy all three counts.
method.columns: 1-based, counted in characters, matching llvm-cov's export for these files
method.final_region: in the body record, the code region (kind 0) that starts exactly at the closing brace (line, column) and ends on the same line, one column later: the one-character `}` exit region.

last_statement.anchor: the token whose region runs on every arrival at the statement: its first token, except for a `for` loop (the iterator expression) and for `let`, `if let` and `while let` (the scrutinee after `=`), whose patterns' regions count iterations or matches

if.region_choice: first region between the anchor and the statement's end

last_statement.expression_tail: no `;` before the closing brace: the tail runs from its first token to the brace, and its anchor is that first token, e.g. `test.assert_is_empty().await` (webdav za_variants::alarm): region [410, 5, 410, 9] contains the anchor (410, 5).
last_statement.if_and_match: the `if` or `match` keyword carries no region of its own; the earliest region inside the statement is the condition or the scrutinee, e.g. [301, 8, 301, 18] for `if failed > 0 { panic!(...) }` in jmap compliance::test. An `if let` is anchored at its scrutinee (see `let`).
last_statement.let: a `let` statement, including `let ... else { ... };`, ends at its `;`; the anchor is the first token of the initialiser after `=`, so a refutable pattern's region (which counts matches) is not used. No sub-test body ends with a `let` at 0.16.27; a loop body that starts with one is anchored the same way (e.g. imap body_structure::test's loop body, anchor (26, 29)).
last_statement.loop: a `for PAT in EXPR { ... }` loop's anchor is the first token of EXPR, the iterator expression, which runs once each time the loop is reached. The pattern's region (before `in`) runs once per iteration, so a loop that iterates zero times would read as not reached; it is not used. A `while COND { }` or `loop { }` uses its first token as the anchor, so the first region inside (the condition, or the first statement of the loop body) counts arrivals.
last_statement.loop_body: for a body whose last statement is a loop, the loop block's first statement is located the same way (its anchor and region choice) and its count is recorded per step: it counts iterations, so a loop reached with zero iterations shows 0 (review M3, ruling 31)
last_statement.passed_over: a statement with no code region in the record (compiled out by a #[cfg], or a tail `async move { }` block whose code is the block's own record) is passed over for the statement before it; a body where no statement has a code region has no count 2, and it is not required. No sub-test body passes over a statement; six helpers do (helpers.functions[].last_statement_passed_over).
last_statement.record_choice: among the records of a step (both binaries, every generic instantiation) the reported one is the first by: executed, then body and exit positive, then the largest body count, then the symbol
last_statement.region: the innermost code region (kind 0) of the body record that contains the anchor (start <= anchor < end; the latest start wins); if none contains it, the earliest code region that starts between the anchor and the statement's end; among regions with that start, the highest count, then the smallest extent (a macro maps its whole expansion onto the call site, and the region that starts the statement runs on every arrival). The exit region is never chosen. At 0.16.27 every chosen region of a sub-test starts at or after its anchor, so none is shared with an earlier statement.
last_statement.splitting: the body between its braces is split into top-level statements at bracket depth 0 of the source with comments and literal contents blanked (baseline-A/tools/laststmt.py). A statement ends at a `;` at depth 0. A block-like statement (`if`, `match`, `for`, `while`, `loop`, a labelled loop, `unsafe { }`, a bare block, a brace macro `name! { }`) ends at its closing brace unless the next token is `else`, `.` or `?`. Items (`fn`, `use`, `struct`, `enum`, `impl`, `const`, `static`, `mod`, `trait`, `type`, `macro_rules!`) are skipped: they run no code in the body. Attributes before a statement stay with it. The last statement that is not an item is the body's last top-level statement.
last_statement.tooling: tests/qualification/tools/strict_rule.py and rustscan.py implement this method (ruling 32); `strict_rule.py self-check` reproduces every recorded region and count from the 5b914ddb5 sources and exports
last_statement.trailing_macro: a macro call statement such as `assert_eq!(...);` or `println!(...);` ends at its `;`; rustc maps the expansion to the call site, so the region that contains the macro name, e.g. [105, 5, 105, 15] for `assert_eq!` in imap messagelimit::test, is the one used.

strict_rule.rule: A call executed in a step only if one function record of that step's export has three positive counts: (1) the sub-test's body record; (2) last_statement, the region that starts the body's last top-level statement; (3) the body's final region. Body record: for an async fn, the async body's own record (never the outer record, which only constructs the future); for a plain fn, the function's own record. Final region: the exit region whose start and end both lie on the body's closing brace (not the region that starts at the opening brace). Count 2 is ruling 7 (coordinator, 2026-10-30): the exit region also counts early returns, the last statement's region does not. A call that completed at 0.16.27 but fails a count gets a completion marker in Task 7 (needs_completion_marker).

rulings.7: the executed rule gains the last_statement count; a call executes in a mode only if all three counts are positive; this tightens the rule and never loosens it
